results.title: The Best Google Analytics Alternative for Developers | Raah | Raah
results.content:
TL;DR

 GA4 is powerful, but many developers and small teams find it too complex for everyday website analytics.
 Simple privacy-first tools are easier to use, but many stop at pageviews, referrers, and basic events.
 Raah is built for teams that want a Google Analytics alternative with traffic analytics, Core Web Vitals, network timing, JavaScript errors, third-party script monitoring, alerts, and status pages.
 Raah does not set cookies or fingerprint users. It focuses on anonymous analytics and real user monitoring signals.
 The free plan includes one project with 100,000 monthly requests and 100,000 monthly user analytics events, so you can start without paying before you know whether it fits. [...] ### Is Raah a Google Analytics replacement?

For many websites, yes. Raah can replace GA4 for pageviews, visitors, referrers, UTM campaigns, Web Vitals, frontend errors, and performance monitoring. If you rely heavily on Google Ads attribution or GA4-specific marketing workflows, you may still need GA4 alongside Raah.

### Does Raah use cookies?

The beacon does not set analytics cookies and uses random browser IDs rather than device fingerprints. Optional identity and payment linking can involve personal data. Browser storage and analytics may require consent depending on the deployment.

### Does Raah slow down my website?

Raah uses a lightweight script-based setup. It is designed to collect analytics and browser performance signals without becoming a heavy client-side dependency. [...] Raah is a strong Google Analytics alternative for:

 Developers who want analytics without GA4 complexity
 Founders who need traffic and product experience in one place
 Agencies managing multiple client sites
 SaaS teams monitoring signup, pricing, and onboarding pages
 Teams that care about Core Web Vitals and frontend reliability
 Privacy-conscious site owners who do not want cookie-heavy analytics
 Vercel, Netlify, and Cloudflare users who want hosting-independent analytics

It is probably not the right fit if your main requirement is Google Ads attribution or enterprise marketing workflows. In that case, GA4 may still need to stay in your stack.

## Ready to switch?

Google Analytics is powerful, but most teams do not need that much complexity just to understand their site.

results.title: Raah vs Plausible | Raah
results.content:
## Main technical difference

Plausible collects event-oriented analytics from the browser: pageviews, referrers, campaigns, goals, and conversion paths. Its data model answers who visited, from where, and which funnel steps completed.

Raah connects revenue attribution, custom events, identified customers, and funnels with traffic, referrers, UTMs, acquisition channels, and a performance telemetry layer: browser fetch and XHR timing, network phases where available, Web Vitals and performance metrics, JavaScript and HTTP errors, third-party domains, and ISP or regional context.
